title: Mixing Units of Measurement
pattern: Representing a physical measurement (time, bytes, distance) as a raw primitive type without explicitly encoding units in the type or parameter names.
why_bad: There is no compiler-enforced check on units. Callers can easily pass milliseconds to functions expecting seconds, or pounds instead of kilograms (e.g. Gimli Glider airplane crash), causing catastrophic calculation or safety failures.
detection: Variables storing units (such as seconds, milliseconds, bytes, kilograms) are declared as raw numeric primitives (i32, f64) without unit wrappers or name tags.
counterexample: Using custom types or encoding the unit directly in the variable name as a suffix: `elapsed_ms`.
fix: Encode the unit suffix in the variable name: `start_ms` and `elapsed_ms`, or use strong units of measure systems.
source: The Art of Readable Code, Chapter 2 (Values with Units) [960-961]; or Code Complete, Section 11.2 & 32.3 [863-864].
